...I’ve grown used to this place.
Oh, it’s all familiar faces here!
Oh, familiar places.
Ah, I’m heading home!
Are we staying here long?
It’s quiet here. Our people are holding this place.
We need to explore the rest of the Zone.
I’ve been here for quite a while.
You could say this is home.
I know a lot of people here—this feels like home, after all.
Hmm, maybe I should stock up...
You never know who you’ll run into here. Too bad most of them want to either eat you or shoot you.
The view from the cooling tower pipe is incredible. You can sometimes hear snippets of radio broadcasts up there, too. That’s how it is.
Kopachi village near the cooling tower is crawling with zombies. And the radiation there is off the charts—the dosimeter sings like a bird!
Want to check out the “Concrete Bath” anomaly? I heard lots of stalkers found a “Soul” there.
See that quarry? The anomaly there is literally called “Quarry.” It’s so toxic, you might not even have bones left.
A helicopter crashed somewhere on the factory grounds... A few years ago the army ran a special operation, but they crashed there—they never made it.
You can reach Pripyat through the underground overpass, but sometimes Monolith and wild animals settle in the technical rooms there.
From the top of the cement factory, you can see the whole area at a glance. Of course, you’ll be visible from a mile away too.
Rumor has it that the “Oasis” might be somewhere beneath the ventilation complex. Do you believe it?

Many stalkers talk about the “Oasis,” but it seems nobody has ever actually seen it.\nOne of our guys said the place is like healing waters—wounds close before your eyes, and your health gets a real boost.
Bandits have holed up at the container depot. Be careful around there.
Want to find out what’s on the factory grounds?
I heard that Strelok spent most of his time around here.
Well, Freedom did take control of Yanov Station after all. I heard Duty and a couple of stalkers rushed into the center, and nobody’s seen them since...
There are all sorts of beasts near the station, so we need to be careful.
Before the 1986 disaster, this area was an important railway station.
My friend told me all sorts of stories about the factory. Mostly about how many mercenaries and bandits who dared to visit it disappeared without a trace...
Do you believe all those stories about the “Heart of the Oasis”?
The railway tunnels are known to be home to dangerous mutants and the Monolith. Honestly, I’d gladly stay away.
I hate swamps so much. Gloom, misery, radiation, and mutants.
There’s a machine yard near the northeastern part. It used to be a Renegade base, but I hear soldiers like to visit it now...
Have you seen the old church? Beautiful and creepy at the same time.
Everyone likes to stash loot in villages and farms... You can always do a little looting, of course.
The Doctor lives somewhere around here. At his age, he hardly ever comes out anymore.
They say a monstrous roar can sometimes be heard at night. Usually somewhere to the west or north.
Marauders keep trying to take over the water tower right next to the stalkers.
The military rarely ventures deep into the bogs, but they do have patrols here, and their orders are to shoot to kill.
A couple of years ago, nobody even knew this place existed, let alone Clear Sky.
Have you ever wondered where exactly the pump sends the water?
Try not to get close to the barbed wire—it wasn’t put up here for nothing. Catch a dose of radiation and you’re done for.
What are we going to do here? Watch Clear Sky dissect frogs?
Dogs are commonplace here. In the tall grass or reeds, you’ll barely spot those mutts.
Stay out of the water, I’m telling you. The radiation is insane.
Nobody knows what might be waiting for us behind those bushes.
We-ell... not as bad as I imagined.
What a swampy place.
Looks like Clear Sky is back on its feet, unlike the Renegades. Still, they got what was coming to them.
Did you know the Swamps weren’t always swamps? There used to be fields, farms, and villages here. Those were the days... Ah, the Zone!
If I’m not mistaken, the pumping station was built to extract anomalous substances from the swamp bottom.
Well, we’ve got a long road ahead.
There’s a camp deep in the forest at an abandoned sawmill—you can rest there and fix up your gear.
There’s sometimes some activity at the gas station.
I recently read that a Controller lives somewhere deep in the forest...
Don’t you find it strange that there are anomalies everywhere here, but hardly any artifacts?
It’s so quiet here that it’s unsettling.
Have you seen all those boxes and crates everywhere? I wonder what happened here...
If only there were a river here... or a little pond. We could fish and have a beer. Ah...
There’s a place somewhere on the edge of the forest where suspicious stalkers have been seen. I don’t feel like checking it out...
There’s an old bridge somewhere beyond the bridge. They say strange things happen there sometimes—you start hearing voices. On the bright side, there’s an anomaly field with artifacts nearby.
I often wonder what happened to the tunnels and where those boulders came from... Could spatial anomalies have caused it?
You know what we really need right now? A damn car. Even a little “hunchback.”
Have you seen the train on the bridge? I wouldn’t want to be there when all that blew up...
I wonder if it’s possible to clear the rubble from the railway tunnels. It would save so much time! And we could shelter from an emission there, too.
Yeah. Pretty lousy place if an emission hits—you’ll be hard-pressed to find shelter.
Honestly, it’s a bleak place, but perfect for smuggling or other shady business. So stay alert.
I have a feeling something is waiting for us behind those trees. We should be careful.
Marauders usually hang around the bridge to ambush unsuspecting victims.
Pseudo-dogs, boars, and fleshes are pretty common around here. I hope we don’t run into the first ones. I wouldn’t mind some of the latter as meat, though.
Looking at this place, it must have been bustling once—there’s even a gas station over there. Now it’s just forest...
We could stay here, of course, but I have no idea who controls this place now.
You can run into military and mercenaries here. Some carry out contracts, others run special operations. It’s best not to get noticed by any of them.
Did you know a helicopter used to patrol this area? It flew right along the road—you couldn’t slip past!
I heard a lot of good stalkers died at this dump.
I’d bet you could rummage through this junk and leave with a full backpack of loot.
They say all kinds of horrors happen here at night. As soon as the sun sets, the stalkers vanish as if blown away.
I heard someone once saw a creature here at night that looked like a chimera or a kikimora. Honestly, I don’t want to choose between those possibilities.
Be careful near the garbage piles in the north of the cemetery—some of them are extremely radioactive.
I recently heard someone has a stash here. In a certain place. Clever, clever.
People often try to smuggle contraband through here, past Duty patrols.
I keep wondering where all these zombified people came from... Could they be coming from Radar?
When was the last emission? It’s a dangerous place if you arrive after one—there’s practically nowhere to hide if another hits. And the graveyard is huge.
There are a couple of towers here with a great view over most of the area, though they also make us an easy target.
This area is so vast that entire squads sometimes disappear without a trace.
Just look at this... What a depressing place.
You look around and think: that’s a lot of scrap metal on the mainland now...
There’s an anomaly somewhere in the southeast. There used to be a little farmstead there, but then “burners” surrounded it and everything burned to hell.
Duty and the bandits have taken a liking to this place, but none of them dares go deeper.
We should avoid the central part of the graveyard—I don’t want to become a bloodsucker’s dinner.
All this equipment glows in the dark. I hope you have good gear and a mask.
Gravity anomalies are extremely common here, so watch where you’re going.
There’s a camp in the northeast. You can wait out a storm or an emission there, or just rest. You never know who else might get the same idea.
They say bloodsuckers come out of their nests here at night...
I’ve heard stories that a chimera has been seen here at night. Scary...
After all, everyone starts somewhere.
Looks like the situation at the northern checkpoint is still unstable.
There used to be a spatial anomaly above the bridge, but then it disappeared...
Did you know they recently found a trail here in the northeast leading to some village with a factory? Not many people know about that place yet.
You can sometimes find artifacts behind the old farm here.
There’s a good spot here by the old locomotive to the east—few stalkers go there, despite the artifacts.
Sidorovich used to work in all sorts of fields. Now he only asks us to get rid of his competitors. He’s getting old...
Cats wander in here sometimes. Ugh, I hate those creatures. Quiet, fast... Once they latch on, they won’t let go.
They say a bloodsucker used to live in the old grain elevator. About five years ago, maybe longer. Sounds like they drove it out for good.
Sometimes you can hear horrible screams and howling at night. I don’t even want to imagine what kind of beast roams in the dark...
Did you know a stalker once stole secret documents from the checkpoint? Of course, everyone denies it, but they say Sidorovich got quite rich afterward.
The Cordon... You know, I wouldn’t mind staying here.
Ah, I remember when there were electro anomalies in the railway tunnel. So many stalkers died trying to get past the checkpoint under the bridge...
Shustry used to run errands for Sidorovich before making a name for himself and heading off to God knows where. Now he’s sitting in some swamp. Quite a career move!
The Ukrainian Armed Forces never managed to stop stalkers from entering the Zone.
I wonder how Sidorovich is doing. I bet he’s still fleecing rookies...
Local stalkers once spotted a bloodsucker by the passage under the railway tunnel. Even here isn’t safe.
What is it, has someone holed up at the vehicle depot again?
I remember the railway bridge being practically a second gateway into the Zone. I doubt the army still controls it.
The grain elevator is a pretty good place to stash loot. Stalkers don’t particularly like setting up camp there.
If I remember correctly, there’s a technician and a trader at the northern farm.
This place is one big dump. Well, you’ve figured that out already.
There’s a Duty outpost in the north, and beyond it lies Rostok. A flea market is nearby—you can find all sorts of goods there and make a bit of money, too.
The part of the Garbage closer to the Dark Valley is pretty dangerous—teeming with mutants and anomalies.
If you’re looking for artifacts, your best bet is the vehicle graveyard or the radioactive swamp across the road.
Duty isn’t too concerned about the northern checkpoint these days. There are patrols, sure, but the men at the post were ordered to leave their positions and fall back to Rostok.
If you go into the toxic bogs, find a suit treated against chemicals or take an antidote. You might get in, but you won’t get out—there’ll be nothing left of you.
There’s a gravity anomaly field out in the sticks. It’s hard to get out alive, so you rarely find artifacts there. You know how it goes—whoever gets there first takes them.
You probably weren’t around back then, but when the guys ran the depot, music blared across the Garbage. It was actually pretty lively. You kind of miss it.
There used to be a so-called “concentration camp” right in the middle of the vehicle lot. The name fit the place. Damn, those were wild times!
I heard you really shouldn’t wander around the trash piles at night. Apparently, bloodsuckers come out to hunt.
Stay away from the garbage piles—there’s radioactive waste galore there!
The depot has all the amenities you need if you get tired or hungry.
So, what are we going to do here, buddy? I’ll say this now: I’m not digging through trash piles.
You never know what you might find in this cemetery...
After the 1986 disaster, everything contaminated was hauled here and to the Vehicle Graveyard.
Mostly stalkers live here, but sometimes bandits wander around looking for easy prey.
You can find artifacts here, of course. But sometimes you spend more on treatment afterward than you get from digging up some anomalous bucket of bolts.
Firefights break out around here pretty often.
Hunters recently set up in the old hangar.
Many stalkers died here... mutants were literally crawling out of the ground. Look, their burrows are still there... creepy!
There must be lots of good stuff in the old industrial complexes.
Just eight years ago, this place was more like the center of the Zone—every kind of mutant was killed here!
By the way, just in case: a helicopter sometimes patrols this area, so keep that in mind if anything happens.
Stay alert in the northern part—every kind of nasty thing comes from Yantar, most often those damn snorks.
I don’t know what they found in the railway tunnel, but I doubt it was barricaded for no reason.

The military know stalkers visit the northern part and the central industrial complex, but usually ignore them. Usually, that is, when the stalkers are smart enough not to provoke the Ukrainian Armed Forces.
You can find a decent haul of gravity artifacts here, but be careful around the swamp—it’s full of nasty things, both animal and anomalous.
You can rest or wait out bad weather in the tunnel or central complex, even an emission.

Bandits tried several times to retake the central complex a couple of years ago, but I heard Sidorovich stepped in and sent someone to deal with them. Now only petty punks hang around the underground.
There are two ways from here to the Garbage: along the road or by the trail in the southeast. The road risks an encounter with punks; the trail, with mutants.
A friend once told me Strelok has a hideout somewhere underground in the local tunnels. I never would’ve guessed! Looks like he picked a good spot.
I remember a huge raid here about six to eight years ago. They even called in paratroopers and special forces. They were hunting some diggers. What a time...
Even though the military’s main base is at the Research Institute, stalkers still come here.
Did you know the Research Institute grounds and building used to be a Duty base? That was before the Big Emission.
Let’s stay away from manholes and underground areas, okay? I’ve heard stories about dangerous anomalies and horrible mutants infesting them... I don’t want to find out whether that’s true or not.
They say some stalker helped Duty flood an underground complex a couple of years ago.
Better stay away from the local swamp and the areas northeast of it—there’s a whole zoo of creatures there.
Ah, I’m getting sleepy... It’s just too peaceful here.
Clear Sky stalkers often pass through this area. There are plenty of anomalies here, and the road to the scientists is close.
What a creepy place... Brr.
You can look for chemical artifacts at the gas station, but you’ll have to be as quiet as a mouse—the bandit base is right across the road.
I’ve been here once before. It was quiet and peaceful then; let’s see how it goes this time.
I remember a full-scale war here a couple of years ago. Freedom even blocked off its checkpoints to keep everyone out.
There’s a place in the southeast that looks like a hole in hell—with fire and all the show that comes with it. There are artifacts too, of course, but you’ll need a good suit.
You know, this place lives up to its name completely.
Ugh, I wouldn’t want to be at the factory at the wrong time...
Lately, some silhouettes have been spotted near the swamp at night. But with the fog, it’s hard to tell what they are.
Contraband is often hauled from here through the Vehicle Graveyard straight to the Warehouses and back.
There are many sewer passages in the Valley, but few know where they lead. Nobody wants to check—this place already has enough sinister secrets.
Borov used to run this place, so it’s no surprise they took him out so quickly.
A couple of stalkers said they witnessed horrible mutants crawling out of the central complex. I believe them—the place was practically made for them!
I was told special forces staged quite a show here a couple of years ago. There were even helicopters.
I think this place has always been gloomy.
There’s supposed to be a lab somewhere around here...
Freedom used to be based here, but after the Big Emission the faction moved to the Warehouses, and bandits took over the northern factory.
We should be careful. Veterans say bandits set up ambushes all over this place.
If you know a safe route, the Vehicle Graveyard makes the Army Warehouses a stone’s throw from here.
You can get to the Cordon pretty quickly via the Glade, completely bypassing the Ravine.
A creepy place. Sometimes nothing happens here, and it still feels eerie and unsettling.
Hey, want to grab a drink at the “100 Rads”?
The bartender is a great guy. He even helped Marked One when he was snooping around those labs.
They say there was a triple murder here, and none of the killers were ever found.
I’ve always wondered why the western part of the factory grounds has been closed all these years... Though perhaps it’s better not to know.
Have you ever wondered why nobody thought to put a tower at the southern entrance? Put a sniper there and no one gets through.
Duty often patrols the road through the Vehicle Graveyard. Contraband flows through there, you see, and the route to the Warehouses is just nearby. They have to keep catching it.
There’s an anomaly in the back here, and it’s literally called that. You could try your luck.
If you’re after adrenaline and money, talk to Arnie about the Arena.
Petrenko often outsources jobs to eliminate enemy targets or mutants. I’d be careful with the former, if I were you.
Have you noticed that Duty has no sniper squads?
Oh, I remember there were stashes in a couple of alleys here. I don’t think anyone really checks them.
That damn loudspeaker! I’ll lose my hearing!
This place is probably the closest thing to the Big Land.
You know that sentry who’s always acting all “move along, stalker”? He gets on my nerves so much, you have no idea.
There’s a guard at the “100 Rads”—a great guy who’s always happy to see me.
I should stock up on supplies from the Bartender. Hope his prices are reasonable today.
I wouldn’t provoke Duty—those guys don’t joke around. They’ll throw you in the lockup or a cage in the Arena. They might even hit you over the head, or remove it entirely if you get too rowdy.
Did you know that people used to be allowed in here only with passes? If the checkpoint guys didn’t like you, that was it—you could forget about this place.
You can get almost any information from the Informant here at the Bar. Not for free, of course. But it’s worth the money.
I once heard that some kind of spy lived in this tower. He even killed someone... They could never catch him. Well, not until the end.
Be careful. This place isn’t called the “Wild Territory” for nothing.
There’s a house here with its roof and the floor beneath it caved in. Looks like a meteorite hit it.
Quiet! Hear that?! Howling... Oh, never mind. False alarm.
You can often find mutts around the loading station. They’re dumb beasts, but they sure are a nuisance.
Veterans told me all kinds of strange things sometimes happen in this place. For example, they said they saw some strange cloud, like soot. And it moved!
A couple of years ago, artifacts used to appear right on the road here! Not like now. The anomalies must have weakened.
If it were up to me, I’d build a proper checkpoint at the passage, with machine-gun nests on both sides and other fortifications. It’d be much easier to hold.
Some kind of ominous place. I don’t even want to know what might be hiding in the workshops and depot—not for any artifacts.

There’s a gate to the south, beyond the railway bridge. You can even walk through it! They say if you know the way, you can easily reach the Garbage without taking a huge detour through Agroprom or the entire factory grounds.
I think there’s a spot by the terminal with electro anomalies and “burning fuzz”... They say you can find artifacts there.
I think people have seen psi-mutants here more than once, so stay alert if you want to live.
Snorks and poltergeists are practically the locals here, so keep your ears open and your eyes peeled.
Duty caught plenty of smugglers here in the past. They kept trying to carry unknown artifacts past the checkpoints.
Seen number 24? It was Wolfhound’s group. A couple of years ago they shot down a helicopter carrying scientists. I don’t know how it all ended, but nobody’s seen Wolfhound since.
I heard stalkers found rare artifacts here. The underground tunnel is known for good artifacts, but the number of electro anomalies in it is off the charts.
Mercenaries are trying to hold the camp near the construction site and the site itself. They succeed with mixed results, I’d say.
Veterans said you can find some of the most dangerous mutants in the Zone here...
The tunnel leading to Yantar is full of burners, and there’s even a “Comet”!
Watch your surroundings carefully, especially between the railcars and cars—snorks usually hang out there.
You can find either valuable artifacts here or instant death.
I think if we rummage through the ruins, we might find some decent stashes.
I wonder if there are real bloodsuckers in this village... Actually, no, no, no. Never mind. Forget I said anything. Let’s move on, okay?
There’s a “Comet” anomaly in the village, so finding roasted stalkers is commonplace.
Skirmishes between different factions and clans happen here all the time.
Some stalkers complain that even outside the Brain Scorcher’s range, this place still weighs on their minds.
An uneasy place. You keep expecting something to happen any moment.
The place is rich in artifacts, which also means armed clashes.
The swamp next to the military base wasn’t this radioactive before. Looks like the latest Big Emission really stirred it up.
You know Cerberus? A veteran loner. One of the few helping to hold the Barrier.
I wouldn’t recommend wandering around the hills south of the village. I don’t know what happened there, but they’re extremely radioactive.
Someone or something is constantly coming from the Vehicle Graveyard. You can barely keep shooting them.
There’s an old farmstead north of the village. When nobody’s holding it, you can set up a decent temporary camp there. Just remember to put up a couple of tripwires so nobody sneaks up on you.
See those stalkers in green camouflage? Freedom. I heard they’re having a hard time holding back the Monolith forces. That’s how it is, man.
The Brain Scorcher and the Red Forest are close by, so there are often plenty of mutants and zombified people around here.
I’d stay away from that village... about two kilometers away.
The Warehouses are bigger than I thought. Freedom picked the right spot, apart from the fanatics next door.
Did you know Freedom drove out the soldiers who survived the Big Emission and took their base?
Mercenaries usually stick to the checkpoint beyond the snork village and rarely venture out. I understand them.
The northern farm is a great place to wait out bad weather or an emission—but only if there aren’t other stalkers or mutants nearby.
Duty usually sends its scouts to the farmstead at the foot of the Freedom base.
Be sure to look up when passing the poles—there’s tons of burning fuzz on them.
I think I can already feel it pressing on my brain.
They say someone here is willing to trade gear and ammo for vodka. That’s a pretty good exchange rate, if you ask me.
Honestly, this place is just disgusting.
I can’t imagine how nobody’s gone crazy here yet, even without any psi emitters.
They say several groups tried to break into the lab. Even Freedom came by to steal some fancy armor.
Around 2011, a group of stalkers managed to reduce the radiation. Then it flared up again. Now that’s what I call building to last.
One of the few places with a damn ton of snorks. Maybe they were created somewhere around here?
Duty fighters used to guard the scientific camp, but then they had to abandon their positions.
I was told this place presses on the mind so much that, for a while, nothing changed even without any brain-scramblers.
They say if you stay near the psi-emission boundary for too long—or venture farther in—all sorts of strange things start appearing.
There’s a huge fire anomaly somewhere behind the factory. I wouldn’t risk going there alone—if anything happens, nobody will help. And if you scream, some snorks will eat you.
There’s a psi emitter somewhere on the factory grounds. But the factory itself is terrifyingly dangerous...
I remember hearing that Sakharov once managed to send a couple of military helicopters to sweep the factory grounds. Truly, still waters run deep!
Let’s not stay here, okay? I don’t want to become a zombie.
When someone mentions Yantar, two things come to mind: zombies and snorks.
When the psi emitter is off, you can go straight to the Dead City without taking the huge detour through Limansk and the Red Forest.
There used to be a big lake here. We could go fishing now...
The notorious X-16 lab is right beneath us. I wish I didn’t know that. God knows what’s going on down there now... that’s why I’m scared.
Some time after the Zone appeared, Yantar was chosen as the ideal location for deploying the mobile research base...\nIf you ask me, it wasn’t the best decision. Agroprom would’ve been better...
When you hear those stories about hordes of zombies here... you start wondering how powerful the psi emitter must be.
The Dead City isn’t called “dead” for nothing. There are zombies everywhere. And Yantar is right nearby...
It feels like you’re in some kind of time anomaly—everything seems lifeless.
It’s like I’ve traveled back in time...
Rumor has it the Monolith forces try to enter the city streets after dark. Just thought you should know.
Yeah, the Zone really didn’t go easy on this place... that’s for sure.
“And Lenin is so young, and October lies ahead!”
You can easily get to the Warehouses from here if you know which branch of the pipe to crawl into. Otherwise, you might end up crawling into a tripwire.
There are supposedly a couple of anomalies here where you can try your luck finding artifacts.
Imagine if zombies came out of every apartment—brrr.
Honestly, this place is so-so. There are plenty of exits, but the neighbors? Limansk, Yantar, the Warehouses—you won’t get bored with neighbors like those.
Dushman’s people are very well supplied, especially if you have money. And especially if they don’t put a bullet in your head instead of talking.
I wonder if there’s anything good inside the buildings...
It’s interesting that the military don’t care about this place at all. It’s as if they don’t even know it exists.
Did you hear a military helicopter was shot down nearby, between this city and Limansk, a couple of years ago? Imagine that...
The mercenaries and bandits still can’t agree on who gets the central square.
The mercenaries’ main base in the Zone is here, in the former cooperative store. They usually don’t let strangers wander near their camp.
Heh. The statue of Vladimir Ilyich is much bigger than I imagined.
Isn’t it ironic that the bandits took over the old school? I hear it literally puts pressure on your brain there, ha-ha.
What an empty city... it’s downright depressing.
A friend told me there’s an extensive sewer system beneath the city. I think the mercenaries use it.
I’ve heard you can run into Monolith troops passing through the city at night.
Why is this place so quiet and creepy? Wait... was that my imagination, or did I hear a child laughing?!
There’s probably something worth looting in these houses, as long as the owners aren’t home.
It feels... strange. Like something is pressing down on me.
See all the barbed wire and barricades around the city? Was the radiation really that bad...?
They say some unknown stalkers were spotted here. Apparently there was even a war...
Stay well away from the river and any water sources—they’re radioactive as hell!
Honestly, I don’t even know if there are any artifact anomalies around here...
There’s probably loot in the basements—unless someone or something gets to us first.
See those antennas? Imagine if they powered them up too... Brr.
Wait, isn’t that Duga? There, see it?
One thing’s for sure: I wouldn’t want to spend the night here.
Ever wonder what you might find inside these buildings?
Maybe we should get out of here?
Veteran stalkers told me there used to be a minefield here. Right in the middle of the street!
They say there’s a whole trap maze in the north of the city. Take one wrong step, or step at the wrong time, and it’ll zap you before you can cry out.
Watch your step and where you’re going, pal. A veteran stalker once told me about forgotten minefields in the city.
The Monolith mostly keep to the north. They have a nearby stronghold there called the Hospital.
I don’t envy the mercenaries—they have to hold the road to Dead City and fight their way farther in.
I have a feeling Monolith will eventually take control of the whole city.
Just look into all those dark windows and you start feeling uneasy...
We should be careful here. There are probably all kinds of traps and tripwires around.
It’s dead quiet...
Maybe we’d better keep our distance from this place?
You can find decent artifacts deep in the woods. Sure you can... Good luck looking!
Keep away from the vehicles on the road—the radiation makes the dosimeter go crazy.
I hear voices in my head...
Did you know Strelok himself shut down this device a couple of years ago?
What a bleak, lifeless place. I don’t even want to imagine what the forest was like before the disaster.
I heard the gates leading to the Red Forest radiate like reactor four.
Just look at this place... No wonder so few dare to push through the Brain Scorcher.
It’s as if the Zone itself made sure no one comes here. The Scorcher is just extra insurance.
What the hell happened here...? Look at those trees... And the bunkers and equipment? A whole base! I’m afraid to imagine what’s going on in the forest.
I’d only ever heard stories about this place... I won’t forget it now.
I’ve got a bad feeling, man. Let’s turn back, okay?
Watch out for anomalies and radiation hotspots—there are enough here to fill the whole Zone!
We’re about to cross the line. Are you sure you know what you’re doing?

In this place, luck can turn its back on you completely—so completely that no one will even know you were here. And if they do find out, it’ll be somewhere at the Barrier. You won’t be around to hear about it, though.
Anyone who gets near the Brain Scorcher goes mad, turns into a zombie, and starts wandering the Zone aimlessly...
Why the hell did we come here, man?! It’s not too late to turn back!
I’m scared, really scared... I’m all tense, God...
Monolith squads can appear here literally out of nowhere.
Monolith patrols the road, and the forest is home to the nastiest mutants. Either way is suicide. Let’s go back, okay?
Did you hear that?! Shh. Keep your eyes peeled, man. Weird stuff happens here.
I heard some unknown stalkers were spotted deep in the forest here.
The Forester can get your gear into top shape. He certainly knows what his work is worth, though.
I’d stay away from the eastern part of the forest. Nothing good ever comes from the Radar side.
Yeah... One of the few places where you can run into chimeras and pseudogiants. Stay alert.
You used to be able to reach Jupiter’s outskirts directly from the bridge checkpoint. Then some stalker collapsed the tunnel. I think it was Meche... no, Strelok! Probably.
I just hope the bridge holds for another ten years. And don’t go near the river—there’s so much crap in it that no anti-rads or antidotes will help.
I remember the mess here back in 2011! They turned the whole area upside down.
You used to be able to reach the Red Forest straight from Yantar, but after one of the Big Emissions the path simply disappeared...
Have you ever listened to the headframe elevator? It’s scary to think what might be going on down there.
This must have been a beautiful nature reserve once...
This forest is home to just about every kind of mutant. Stay alert!
You have to look for the bright side, even in a dump like this. At least there are no mutant ticks here. We have enough bloodsuckers already—Sidorovich alone is plenty!
Luck can abandon you completely in this place—so completely that no one will even know you were here.
Maybe we should visit the Forester and have a drink or two?
The forest is crawling with anomalies—on the ground, in the air, in the trees. Damn!
Many stalkers fell at the reserve’s main gate... This place was never peaceful.
You can find good artifacts in the old mines, but you can also disappear without a trace.
Did you know the Symbiont anomaly lies deep in the forest? It looks like two giant claws sticking out of the ground.\nIf the rumors are true, you can find artifacts of almost any kind there.
Need a guide? Freedom is to the south, Monolith comes from Radar, bandits are by the bridge, and stalkers gather near the Forester’s tower.\nWelcome to the Red Forest!
This place feels wrong... Don’t you think someone’s watching us from the windows? No? Exactly...
Damn. Why did I agree to come here...?
Ugh, I feel uneasy here...
Is it just me, or can I hear children singing?
The atmosphere is oppressively eerie. It feels like someone still lives in all these apartments.
We should be careful here.
Stick close to the buildings—you could catch a bullet in the middle of the street.
I can still hear that accursed announcement in my head...
Ah, what a beautiful city this must have been before the disaster...
I wonder what the view is like from the rooftops...
I heard the military lost a couple of birds here during the assault on the Chernobyl plant. They went down right in the city.
Just look at all this...
Take my advice: keep a close eye on the rooftops.
I wonder if there are any artifacts here. We are in the center of the Zone, after all.
A city built for the engineers who worked at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant... Just think about it.
This used to be a lively place... Now it’s a ghost town, inhabited only by mutants and Monolith.
The famous Ferris wheel... damn, it’s even bigger than I imagined. And it must be radioactive..!
Looks like Avangard Stadium has become one big battlefield between Monolith and the military.
Coming here was your best idea?! Maybe we should head back before it’s too late, man?
We’re behind enemy lines, pal. I hope you know what you’re doing... I really hope so.
Get ready to meet the enemy. They could show up any moment. Check the windows, rooftops, and entrances.
I... I can’t believe my eyes... The plant! We’ve reached the center!
So, shall we look for an artifact bonanza?
Wait, I’ll mark our route here on my PDA. You don’t make it to the Chernobyl plant alive every day!
I’m still alive... I am alive, right?
I... I can’t believe my eyes... The plant! We’ve reached the center!
So, shall we look for an artifact bonanza?
Wait, I’ll mark our route here on my PDA. You don’t make it to the Chernobyl plant alive every day!
I’m still alive... I am alive, right?
There it is—the Chernobyl plant—right in front of us... I can’t believe it...
We made it... Looks like there was a whole war here...
After everything we’ve been through, we finally made it!
The center... we finally made it to the center, can you believe it?!
I’ve never been this nervous!
Stay calm and keep your eyes open—the Monolith could be anywhere.
God... What happened here?!
There it is—the Chernobyl plant—right in front of us... I can’t believe it...
We made it, at last! Damn, looks like there was a whole war here...
After everything we’ve been through, we finally made it!
The center... we finally made it to the center, can you believe it?!
I’ve never been this nervous!
Stay calm and keep your eyes open—the Monolith could be anywhere.
God... What happened here?!
What an empty, ominous place...
The Yubileiny service center is probably the biggest building in this part of the city. That’s why Monolith has made itself at home there.
There are a couple of accessible sections of the underground passages here. You can hide from pursuers if needed.
Heard there was a whole war here in 2012? Military birds landed right in Monolith’s nest. The stories veterans told me about it...
Huh?! What was that?! Damn, must’ve imagined it... Sounded like someone whispered in my ear. What the hell!
Better stay away from the emergency hospital—there are either mutants or some shady stalkers hanging around.
Do you think there’s a way to get onto a roof around here?
I know someone who was born right here. Shame he’s busy with his own affairs.
At night, this place must turn into a complete hellhole. It’s always like that! By day it seems harmless, but at night...
If it were up to me, I’d bring some tools and set up a stash on the top floors of one of these high-rises.
I wonder what kind of mutants live in the river...
Think we should check the buildings for anything good? Stashes, artifacts, that sort of thing...
Imagine being alone in the city when the very first emission hits! After that, no one would even remember you.
This was once a city built for the engineers who worked at the Chernobyl plant.
This used to be a lively place... Now it’s a ghost town, inhabited only by mutants and Monolith.
I heard one of the secret X-labs is somewhere in the city. Can you imagine? Do you think the residents knew?
The former laundry building has become a refuge for the stalkers who managed to sneak into the city.
What a confusing place—it’s downright terrifying! Wait, where did we even come from?! Oh, hell...
Garik said Monolith had a psi-emitter in the garden here. Good thing it’s gone now.
Look, there’s a department store and a grocery nearby. Shall we stock up?
Another swamp in the Zone... Well, hello there.
I heard that almost every stalker who entered the Krug research institute disappeared. Creepy.
There’s a guy here called Noah, by the way. A friend told me he tamed a pseudodog—can you believe that? I won’t believe it till I see it myself!
Better stay away from the gas station—mutants hang around there pretty often.
The Claw anomaly in Zaton is probably the biggest of its kind, not to mention the goodies inside. If only there weren’t snorks... Sigh!
Have you ever wondered how the Scar formed? Look at a satellite image of the area. It raises so many questions your head spins...
The Circus anomaly lives up to its name: two “comets,” a bunch of anomalies below, and bouncing artifacts... What a show! You’ll need a SEVA suit or a scientist’s suit to get in, though.

Iron Forest is packed with electrical anomalies, and poltergeists live there too. I heard a poltergeist threw a barrel at a stalker and sent him straight into an electro. Quite a sight—and the stench was something else. I think someone even threw up.
We could find all kinds of artifacts here... and anomalies... and mutants... Listen, let’s not just stand around, okay? This place gives me the creeps.
It feels so bleak...
Did you know the stalkers on the Skadovsk kicked the bandits out for good?
Zaton is also called the “old riverbed”... makes sense.
You can ride out an emission in these big ships if one hits.
I guarantee there’s something worth taking in those trucks on the Preobrazhensky Bridge.
The mercenaries still hold the waste processing plant. They don’t waste words with lost souls.
Seen the sawmill? It’s deserted, except for the occasional zombie wandering around.
Damn, I’m getting hungry.
That last emission really shook us up.
It’s nice finding forgotten bolts in your pockets. You never know when you’ll need them.
...I should’ve hidden my loot somewhere else. They’ll find it sooner or later, guaranteed.
Lately, stalkers have been disappearing without a trace pretty often... The Zone.
Hey, $name, are you rich? Looks like it.
Ah, I could use a drink.
I miss my family and old friends.
That’s life in the Zone.
Anomalies everywhere... Watch your step, $name.
Stay away from psi-fields. I don’t plan on becoming a zombie.
Yeah, I'm getting a bit tired.
The encyclopedia says, “Pseudodogs are mutants descended from wolves”... so why are they called pseudodogs?
I should've sharpened my knife... I'll definitely need it, and it's so dull I can only cut butter with it.
If there's one thing I never want to see in my life, it's a chimera... Brrr.
Damn, did you hear that growl?! This is bad, buddy.
We need to stick together, $name. I'll cover you if anything happens.
Maybe it's none of my business, but will you tell me what brought you to the Zone, $name?
They say psydogs can control other people's minds. Can you believe that? I have no plans to become a chew toy for their pups.
Heard the stories about dark stalkers? They hide in the shadows, ambush stalkers, and drag them off to who knows where. No one ever sees them again...
So, what do we do next?
What are your plans, $name?
They say burers were the result of secret experiments on criminals.
I was told pseudogiants are the result of failed experiments in one of those labs...
I hope we don't run into anything nasty along the way.
I need a new pistol; mine's starting to rust.
Anyone know if an emission is coming soon?
Keep your eyes peeled.
So, shall we send those Ichthyanders on their final voyage?

...My blood type on my sleeve,
My serial number on my sleeve.
Wish me luck in battle.
Wish me
Not to be left in this grass...
See that tushkan? ...Neither do I. But it's there!

...And two thousand years of war.
A war without a particular reason.
War is for the young.
A cure for wrinkles...
Got anyone waiting for you back home, brother? My wife is waiting for me, a real beauty...

You lured me in,
You let me down;
You drove me, a young man,
Right out of my mind!
One good thing, brother: no need to pack anyone into plastic bags.
I heard they used to send rookies into Agroprom's underground. Damn, what did you have to do to get that assignment...
Damn, I left an extra ration in my stash... Should've taken it after all.

Heard of Khaletsky? We had a major by that name before Kuznets... People say a lot about him, and he really was a complicated man. At least he hated desk rats. Nobody likes those. They live it up in there... while each day out here gets worse.
I have orders to shoot to kill if I find any unregistered persons.
There are quite a few of our guys in Duty. A couple of years ago, they even had an SBU recruiter there; maybe he's still around.
Ugh, I'd send every one of those monochrome bastards to the other side, then hunt them down there too! We lost good men at Monolith and Fairway because of those deranged assholes.

Duty practically gave us their Agroprom base. By then they'd regained access to Rostok, but one of those freak emissions in 2011 killed most of their men right at the base. Even our commanders at the Institute sometimes pay their respects to the brothers.

About eight years ago, a Big Emission hit our main base at the Warehouses so hard it killed half the men and zombified the rest. Then those Freedom bastards came like jackals to finish off the survivors. I hate those freaks.
I wouldn't wander the Zone at night, brother. All kinds of things crawl out—it's terrifying!
We must prevent unauthorized persons from entering the Zone.
We should restock our medical supplies. I think they brought fresh stock to the base yesterday.
Brother, if you need a job or a side gig, talk to the commander—he always has plenty of problems that need sorting out.
Being a soldier sucks. Being a soldier in the Zone is twice as bad.
Ah, damn... I left my lighter back at camp.
We definitely need to take out all those stoners.
I really want to go home... I'm sick of this Zone, brother.
Sultan's offering a side job. We should check out what he's got.
Bro, I'm telling you, those clowns who took over the depot haven't seen real life.
One of the boys came back from Agroprom underground recently. The shit he told us... scared me straight. Screw those tunnels. Picking off suckers on the Cordon is more my thing.
Man, I hate those Duty cops. They just won't leave us alone. I'd shove every one of the bastards onto a bottle.
You can make good money selling colorful snork trophies to Maslin. Only those freaks usually have guards, and the guards carry serious guns.
Those Duty punks think they run the place... Ha, dumb as hell. Even stalkers kick their asses sometimes.

Those Monolith bastards are completely unhinged. The boys once tried to bribe them, planning to sell out some rookie stalkers in exchange for guns or decent gear. What do you think, $name? They killed both the stalkers and our guys for nothing, the bastards. No emotion at all. Like... what are they called? Robots, yeah.

Freedom... Duty... They're both shit, if you ask me. At least the greens can get you weed and heroin. The cops? They'll roll you into a joint themselves and hand you over to their Arena or the Duty boys. Unless they put a bullet between your eyes first.
Those Freedom peacocks and their “true blues” keep whining about lawlessness. What a bunch of clowns, huh?
$name, give me a heads-up if some fat mark shows up, alright?
Feel like shooting up some suckers... What do you say?
Got word from the boys—they're watching for marks at the Garbage. Heh, let's see what those suckers brought us.
I recently took down such a sucker. It was a real sweet deal. Yeah, damn...
Hey, $name, got a smoke?
The boys once organized a hunt. What a sight, buddy. Those hunting dogs were hilarious—you've never seen mutts like them, I swear.
Damn, where'd I lose my lighter?! This sucks.
I was thinking, buddy: what's the point of messing with all this artifact crap if you can't even spend the cash on a girl later? That's how it is.
Come o-o-on!\nChiki-briki, into the kings!
Bro, got anything to drink?! Even a little ampoule?
When I get back to the boys, we should fleece those suckers—stalkers' pockets are always full of loot, heh.
Our guys say Kholod has a job for us. What do you think? Shall we pay him a visit?

The Professor and Sakharov found that artifacts can appear after a psi-storm too. If only I'd known sooner! I walked past anomalies so many times after storms without even taking out my detector. What an idiot, huh?
It gets kind of sad when you think of the guys from 2011 and what happened to them. A real wave of grief comes over you.
Those renegades are at it again... Renegades... They're traitors, that's what they are!
I think Scar might have been lucky. The Zone did something to those spheres of his to protect him from emissions... What do you think?
You know the Zone is full of secret labs? The guys sometimes break into them to retrieve documents.
Ah, I'd get myself a pseudodog. It'd guard me faithfully and scare off bandits, and you barely need to feed it!
They say Monolith has a weapon resembling one of our old electromagnetic designs. It'd be frightening if that's true.
Why do you think the army's gone crazy and pushed into the Swamps? There's nothing here but bogs and an old pumping station.
Somewhere in the north of the Swamps lives the legendary Doctor. A good old man. He might even bring you back from the dead and ask for nothing in return.
Honestly, I like Kholod more than Lebedev.
You know what they say: what doesn't kill you makes you stronger. I think we'll not only regain our former strength, we'll build on it.
The radiation in the Swamps... somehow sinks from the surface into the bogs, but the Professor hasn't figured out why yet.
We need to stay alert, or we'll run into a mugging. There's plenty of that around here...

Ever wonder what happened to Lebedev and the others after the Big Emission? Kholod says they died. But I heard they became Monolith soldiers... \nThey might still be alive. I wonder if they can be brought back to their senses...

- Phew... I nearly shit myself. Or maybe I did. 
- I’ll find that Raccoon and shove his detector somewhere...

- Buying a map of safe paths to Dead City! Paying well! 
- Brother, save your money. Maps drawn before the Superemission are good for nothing but toilet paper now. 
- Where can I get new ones? 
- Nowhere. Small groups wander blind; whoever survives becomes the cartographer. 
- Yeah, I bought a route from a "guide". Ended up at a burner field the size of a football stadium that had never been there before. 
- Welcome to the new Zone, old man.

- Heard a huge pack of pseudogiants roams near the Center. One is especially big, like their leader. I haven't seen it, so I don't know... hard to believe.. 
- If you don't believe it, go check. Why post nonsense? 
- Are you stupid? If you care, check yourself. Don't act so smart. 
- BAdmin: no fighting, guys. One-hour timeout for both.

- Hey, what are those new creatures... almost skinless, moving completely silently? 
- Mutated Fractures, maybe? 
- No. A Fracture screams loud enough to make your ears ring. This one just stood in the bushes watching. Not a sound. I emptied a magazine into it; it didn’t even flinch, just dissolved into the shadows. 
- Quit smoking Freedom’s weed. 
- I’m serious! My hands are still shaking. 
- If it’s a spawn of the Gloom, we’re done for. A normal mutant at least wants to eat; who knows what these things want...

- Selling a custom exoskeleton, condition 4/5, servos intact, improved anomaly protection. Price: five tier-three artifacts or equivalent cash. 
- Are you insane?! For that money I could bring you an armored vehicle from the Big Land! 
- Don’t like it? Walk around in your underwear. No more supplies from the North, warehouses are empty. Want to live through the Superemission? Pay up. 
- Damn profiteers... 
- He’s right. Decent gear is worth its weight in gold now. Those who were too late are food.

- Do the scientists beyond the Perimeter even respond? 
- Only on closed channels. Passed a bunker yesterday: blast doors welded shut, new turrets on the roof. 
- Afraid of something? 
- Mutants move in packs after an emission. Recently they wiped out an army checkpoint without breaking a sweat. Scientists won’t come out now. 
- If the eggheads shut themselves in, we’ll have no medicine or jobs. 
- Learn to put plantain on your ass, rookie.

- Guys, anyone know why electric anomalies glow dark blue instead of light blue now? 
- The Zone’s physics changed, that’s why. Just don’t go near them. 
- I threw a bolt; it didn’t bounce, it got pulled in and melted in a second! 
- It’s a “Magnetic Electra,” some new shit. They say metal plates in your armor will attract it and it’ll fry you like a sausage in a microwave. 
- Damn!.. So we have to take off the suit? 
- Without it, a kikimora will eat you. Pick what you want to die from.

- SOS! Square... *static* ...we’re surrounded! About twenty creatures! ... *screams* ...it’s eating me! IT’S EATING ME! 
- Who’s on the radio?! Give us your coordinates! 
- ... *ripping metal and a rasp* no... careful!... here... 
- Damn it. The signal’s gone. 
- Rest in peace, I guess. 
- BAdmin: Signal lost from a seven-person group. Red Forest area. Avoid this square until the next Superemission. 
- Great, I guess I’m turning back to the shelter...

- Guys, I saw something strange today. Purple flashes over the Gloom, right inside the black fog. 
- Hallucinations again? 
- No, I watched through optics from a safe distance. Like a storm, but silent. After each flash my detector went crazy, readings jumping all over. 
- The Zone is breathing, lad. The Superemission was only the beginning. 
- Don’t jinx it. We’ve got enough problems. 
- Stay away from the Center. Nobody survives there now.

- Looking for a partner to hike into Dark Hollow. Must be fit and have an empty rig. 
- Why do you need a partner without ammo? 
- To carry loot. I shoot, he carries. 
- Brilliant. What if you miss? 
- Then he runs off and distracts the mutants while I leave with the loot.)) 
- Get lost, you shitty “strategist.” 
- Smart guys like you are why real stalkers go missing. 
- No one’s forcing you; I’m just making an offer. 
- Don’t broadcast your signal, or the boys may “offer” you something else.

- Don’t take jobs clearing underground labs. Yesterday two teams went into X-18 and X-16. Both vanished. 
- People always vanished there. Nothing new. 
- No, listen. Their beacons showed strange readings before contact was lost. Pressure and temperature jumped as if they’d fallen into a volcano’s throat. 
- Has the Gloom reached underground too? 
- Looks like it. Underground is worse than the surface now. 
- Every day gets more fun.

- Anyone tried going into the Bar? Duty’s warehouses have enough loot for life! 
- Go on, try. Snork nests in every hangar now. The Arena’s packed with pulsing biomass. 
- I watched from Rostok’s roof last week. You can’t see asphalt, just mutants. 
- Forget the Bar. It’s gone, just one huge feeding ground. 
- They want to open a place on the outskirts called “Last Drop.” 
- Great, can’t wait.)

- Be careful at shelter airlocks at night. Someone knocked yesterday, asking to be let in with Stepka’s voice. 
- Did you let him in? 
- Stepka died three days ago, torn apart by an anomaly before my eyes... The outside camera showed a tall, unnatural creature opening its mouth. It had Stepka’s voice. 
- Damn... they copy voices now? 
- Stay quiet and don’t open the door to just anyone.

- Hey, folks, what’s going on with the military? They’ve gone completely nuts, walking around shooting everywhere like psychos...
- They’ve taken losses among the research teams, didn’t you hear? Mutants ate a couple of important brains, so now they’re trying to “clean house with a fork.”
- Damn, if even the military can’t handle it, what’s going to happen next?
- Nothing. What difference does it make to you? Just keep your own backside warm.
- Fair enough.

- Buying a Medallion! Urgent! Need radiation protection, paying double. Send coordinates privately! 
- Good luck. Old artifacts mutated after the Superemission. A Whirlwind in my container became stinking slime. 
- True, many lost their properties. Find fresh ones if you want to live. You know where to look. 
- BAdmin: Selling “rotten” artifacts online gets you banned and your signal exposed. 
- I’m serious, I’ll buy anything against radiation!..

- What’s that stuff falling from the sky? Some kind of black ash. 
- It’s blowing in from the Gloom. The wind carries it. Keep it off your skin—it causes chemical burns that itch down to the bone. 
- After the storm, this crap clogged the ventilation filters in our shelter. We opened them up and the filter had melted to hell. 
- Wear closed-cycle breathing gear or keep your gas masks on until the cloud passes. 
- Great, now the air is killing us too. Love this hole.

- He calls... warm, dark... we’ll all become one... 
- Oh, another one’s lost his mind. Someone cut off his PDA, this is making me sick. 
- ...there is no pain inside the Gloom... come... open the doors... 
- BAdmin: Peilung blocked, ID removed from the network. 
- Fast work. Where was he, exactly? 
- BAdmin: Two kilometers west of your shelter, square C-2. 
- Oh, for fuck’s sake...

- Attention on the network! The remnants of the Orion group offer perimeter-clearing around shelters. Payment in gear or artifacts. 
- Mercs cleaning mutant shit now? What a time to be alive. 
- What did you expect? Fewer jobs from the Big Land, no choppers flying. Everyone needs to eat. 
- Sure, let them clear the perimeter and they’ll cut you down for supplies. We’ve seen that before. 
- Your choice, little dead men. At least we’re professionals, not meat.

- Anyone know how to break into a mobile science lab? Found one, locked tight from inside. 
- Try thermite. But why the hell go in? If they sealed themselves in, it must be safe. Let them stay. 
- I looked through a window. Blood everywhere, bodies in lab coats in the corners. No bullet holes outside, doors intact. They killed each other. 
- The Gloom got through even lead walls... 
- Exactly. So, anyone have thermite? I need their equipment. 
- You’re a shameless looter. 
- What’s wrong with that?..

- Guys... I have two magazines of ammo left and no filters. I’m in an attic in Limansk; something’s howling below... dozens of them. 
- Send coordinates. Maybe someone’s nearby and can handle it with a heavy-caliber gun. 
- Who’d bother? Just... if anyone gets out of this hellhole to the Big Land, tell them we weren’t all bastards here. 
- Hang on, man! Don’t put the gun in your mouth! You hear me?! 
- ... 
- Hey?! 
- BAdmin: Peilung cut off. Guess that’s it...

- Heard the Freedomers tried to retake their base on Military? 
- How’d it go? 
- Badly. They gathered their remaining people and attacked with heavy weapons. But chimeras had nested there. They killed half of them, then one showed up... black, with armored growths. 
- Alpha hybrids? 
- Hell if I know. Not even bones were left of the squad. Freedom’s basically gone as a faction; they scattered into shelters. 
- Good riddance, you potheads. 
- Shut up. Ideology can wait. I feel sorry for the people.

- Where do bodies go after an emission? 
- They rot or mutants eat them. 
- That’s the thing: they don’t! A sniper killed a bandit yesterday and left him in a ravine. Today: no blood, body, or gear. He evaporated; no drag marks. 
- The Zone cleans itself. 
- The Zone eats us; the Gloom digests us. Soon nothing living will remain. 
- What a philosopher. Change the generator filters instead.

- Heard about the fight at the Garbage? 
- What happened? 
- Scientists hauled another mega-prototype-of-the-universe; mercs attacked. One idiot fired a grenade launcher, sending the eggheads flying. 
- You’re kidding? Mercs are friends with scientists! 
- Fool. Mercs are friends only with Ben Franklin. Remember. 
- What about the fight? 
- Mercs killed everyone and went west. No scientists survived. 
- Damn, all of them? 
- That prototype had something important. People are killed over it...

- Saw mercs heading west from the Garbage? 
- So what? First time seeing them? 
- They started shooting like crazy, fully kitted, probably thermal optics—they spotted me in the bushes! 
- Thermal optics at the Garbage... elite team on a big contract. 
- Elite my ass. 7.62 goes through anyone; don’t miss. 
- Hero in a hole. That round will go through you before you squeak. 
- West... where? 
- Probably the same mercs who killed the scientists. 
- What difference now? Even the bodies are gone. 
- True. Let’s remember them.

- Guys! Rumor has it a bunch of veteran stalkers have returned to the Zone. What do you think?
- What’s there to think about? New anomalies are producing artifacts nobody’s seen before. People are coming to make some money.
- Sure, except they’re shit out of luck. The Zone’s no resort now, Kalashnikov up my ass. You could make a decent living before... but now? Too many monsters and too many bastards.
- What, someone robbed you, grandpa? Yeah, yeah, go have a cry.
- BAdmin: Well, look at that, we’ve got an outlaw here! I sent the coordinates; someone deal with him if you can be bothered.
- Tungsten here. Job accepted.
- Ooh, that’s it for the poor bastard. Let’s remember him...

- Found the site on the Garbage. Damn. Their “prototype” was a melted crater and scraps of blue plastic. 
- Bodies? Documents? 
- Bodies stripped clean. Burned papers everywhere, but not all were destroyed. Fresh tracks showed a crate dragged toward Agroprom. 
- Toward the Institute? That’s the lair of those things with extra limbs. 
- Mercs must be desperate. The crate probably held the valuable stuff, since they took it.

- Saw mercs at the Garbage–Agroprom crossing. Mad as dogs. 
- Did they go into the complex? 
- No, that’s the weird part. They passed the gate and went south. You get it. 
- Wonder where they ran off to... 
- Maybe a temporary den. Strange there aren’t more mercs at Agroprom... only a couple wandering around. 
- Yeah...

- Hey, big guys) I got info from a private chat: “Inf: Contract to seize prototype failed, code H-33-From_Window-16-2.” Thoughts? 
- Whoa, the Informant got hacked? So what now, the client gets nothing? 
- Inf: Damn it... 
- BAdmin: Inf, calm down, I muted it and will have a word with you. Your “contractors” blew up half the Garbage yesterday; everyone knows already. 
- Inf: No comment. 
- Folks, “From_Window-16-2” is old Agroprom digger slang. Interesting, hmm.

- Hey, guys, our radio picked up a strange signal at Agroprom. 
- A code? 
- Seems so. Mercs talking, arguing about “the toilet won’t flood without the loot,” or something. 
- Your merc’s an idiot. They blew up the loot themselves at the Garbage, but what “toilet” means is still a mystery, haha. 
- Where are they holed up? 
- No idea. Radiation west, swamps south, anomalies everywhere north... nowhere for mercs to settle. 
- Yet they’re still chatting on the air.

- Hey, wanderers. I visited the Garbage firefight site. Good lord. There’s a crater from a VOG and lots of metal fused into the asphalt. 
- They wrecked the device? Idiots. 
- Yeah, some merc fired an underbarrel at close range. I saw tracks—they hurried west. 
- Listen, you lousy Sherlock, keep talking and you’ll end up in the ground. 
- Is that a threat? 
- A warning. You’re broadcasting your signal, and it’s not just stalkers here. 
- Got it.

- Be careful if you go west, where the two old factories stand. Saw a squad of “blues” there, mean as hell. 
- Did they go to the buildings? There’s nothing there, mutants ate it all. 
- No, they didn’t enter. 
- Maybe they went into the sewers?! 
- What sewers? It’s all collapsed. Even if there’s an underground passage, there are enough mutants for a zoo. 
- Rumor said three months ago they had a cache underground. 
- Sure, a cache, and a goldfish in it. You believe everything.

- Anyone heard about the guy who came back from the Darkness? They say he didn’t say a word, just walked, sat by a fire, and started gouging out his own eyes. Quiet as you like. Creepy as hell.
- Keep believing every campfire story and you’ll get smarter, sure.
- Another joker, eh? You never go farther than Agroprom, do you? Better safe than sorry. Jokers don’t live long, I’m telling you.
- We recently lost a joker too. Maybe it’s a pattern, maybe not, but every upbeat guy I knew died sooner than the rest.
- Same damn thing happened in our camp.

- There’s this guy hauling absolutely everything around: junk, suits, broken guns, even a second backpack. Like a lunatic.
- Seen it. Dragon sickness, they call it.
- Those guys don’t last. In the Center, any useless extra weight is a problem.
- Why?
- You won’t have the strength to run. Think you can kill every mutant? What if a whole pack catches you? Right, you’ll feed them.
- Don’t say that!

- Seriously now. Heard of Alpha Hybrids? New kinds of mutants, never seen before.
- Yeah. A merc squad was hired to pack up the guts of one and send them to the mainland.
- Did they manage it?
- Sure: they packed up the mercs’ guts. We found their signal—eight fighters in exoskeletons, smeared across the road.
- Holy shit. Those mutant guts must be worth a fortune.
- Son, take my advice: run if you see one.
- I know one man who saw a hybrid. He survived only because he left his friend behind as bait.
- Damn...

- Any word on square D-4-2?
- The approaches are mined, observers are posted, last check was two hours ago.
- We should send another team before the Super-emission.
- Uh... guys, this is a public channel.
- What the hell...
- Well, D-4-2, huh...
- Guys, I accidentally pasted that. Anyone from our side going to D-4-2, watch out for mines.
- Send the info to the Bartender; he’ll update the maps. You’d be doing everyone a favor.
- Sure, I’ll send it now!
- Thanks, kind sir. Good luck.
- Really, thanks. I nearly blew up on the trail yesterday; good thing my PDA beeped.

- Hey, why are there fewer of those Duty-Free weirdos around?
- First, you’re the weirdo. Second, they took massive losses.
- That many died?
- When the first Super-emission hit, everyone in the north turned into vegetables. Those wooden huts didn’t save them.
- Damn, seriously?!
- Kid, did you fall off the Moon? It’s been a meat grinder here for three months, and you’re still dreaming in pink.
- Leave him be, he only arrived last week.
- Heh, fresh meat, walking right in.
- BAdmin: One-day mute. Good luck, rookie.
- Amen, bartender-bro!

Inf: Request M-131-45-16-81-C, triple rate. 
What the hell is that? 
Probably an evacuation request. 
Yeah, some guy must’ve paid the Informant for the top-tier insurance.)) 
Things must be bad. Any info on who placed the order? 
Eighth, received. 
Oh, there’s the contractor. 
Damn, can I get one like that too? 
Sure, but you can’t afford it, old man. 
BAdmin: Inf, didn’t I set up a dedicated line for you? 
Inf: It’s urgent. 
BAdmin: Fine, no problem.

I listened to a stalker from Sin. I’ve realized a lot: I’ve brought so much evil into the world, even unintentionally, all because of people’s stupid greed. Artifacts... money... No, none of that matters. I don’t want to lose my soul in this endless cycle. I’ll save up for better gear and join the mission of the sinful stalkers.

Hey, has anyone met that shady Stalker who never shuts up and preaches? He kept pestering me about his clan, saying I should join and learn the truth. Sure, the truth... What the hell is this?! I swear, people get dumber every year. Is it the radiation frying their brains? As if the Stone crazies weren’t enough, now we’ve got these damn “dark stalkers.” Pah!

Listen to this: “We are heralds of a new era. We will reveal truth and purification to the world. We will give everyone paradise.”\nSome Stalker was spouting exactly that nonsense to me a couple of hours ago. Who the hell is he? What do you think, should I have... dealt with him, just in case?
Heard about another Stalker group? They call themselves Sin. True or not, I doubt anything good will come of them... Stay alert, guys.

Hunters report seeing some shady Stalkers in the woods calling themselves Sin. They looked creepy as hell and spouted nonsense. They didn’t shoot, but the guys still got away from that “Sin” fast. Either crazy or some kind of cultists... as if Monolith wasn’t enough!
Have you also met some sniveler wandering through camps and pushing his “Let’s talk about the Zone” pamphlets? I don’t get it—does the Zone have honey smeared everywhere to attract fanatics?
I heard bandits recently jumped some Stalkers with unknown patches. They looked terrifying, too. They say the bandits barely escaped those freaks.
Damn! Either I got bootleg vodka, or it’s time to quit. I ran into some preacher going on about the Zone, the universe, and humanity’s vices. Yeah, definitely time to quit...

That’s it, guys. I’ve thought it over and decided it’s time to change my life. I’ll either leave the Zone or join these Sinners. That Stalker was right: we’re all here for our base desires—even Freedomers, who claim they want to free the Zone, though the Zone never asked them to.

All I find are rocks and trash. Well, no... yesterday I found an abandoned bottle of vodka. At least it flushed out the radiation...
It happens.
Congratulations twice, buddy! First, on finding the artifact! Second, on your new enemies...\nWhat were you idiots thinking, announcing it to the whole Zone?!
